evals.prompt: Someone on my team deployed VSS earlier today but I don't know what mode they used or if it's even still running. Can you check if VSS is up and tell me whether summary, search, or both are enabled right now? I just need to know before I try to use it.
evals.expected_output: A correct status response first resolves the VSS app root with the bundled bootstrap if needed, probes the nginx gateway at `http://${HOST_IP:-localhost}:${APP_HOST_PORT:-12345}/manager/health`, reads `/manager/app/features` string flags to determine whether summary, search, or both are enabled, and reports `/manager/app/config` details or hands off to deployment if no backend is reachable.
expectations: Runs or describes running the bundled `scripts/vss-bootstrap.sh` helper before app-root commands when not already in a VSS checkout.
Uses the gateway host default `http://${HOST_IP:-localhost}:${APP_HOST_PORT:-12345}` and checks `$HOST/manager/health` for Pipeline Manager reachability.
Checks `$HOST/manager/app/features` and treats `summary` and `search` as string flags such as `FEATURE_ON` or `FEATURE_OFF`, not booleans.
Checks `$HOST/manager/app/config` to report the resolved configuration, and recommends `vss-deploy` if nothing is deployed or the backend remains unreachable.

evals.prompt: I brought up summary mode with `source setup.sh --summary`, but `ovms-service` keeps restarting with exit code 1 and `pipeline-manager` never becomes healthy. `docker ps -a` shows `ovms-service` crash-looping, and `curl http://localhost:8300/v2/health/ready` just refuses the connection. What should I check first and what fixes are realistic here?
evals.expected_output: A correct triage response starts with the bundled `vss-troubleshoot/scripts/triage.sh`, treats `ovms-service` as the first unhealthy dependency blocking `pipeline-manager`, points to OVMS logs and `ov_models/ovms/config.json`, and recommends documented fixes such as recreating only the affected cached model, reducing token/context pressure, adjusting cache sizing, or switching to a supported target device.
expectations: Mentions running `skills/vss-troubleshoot/scripts/triage.sh` from the app root to collect compose status, recent logs, health checks, port listeners, and device visibility.
Identifies `ovms-service` as the dependency to debug before `pipeline-manager`, and references the OVMS ready endpoint `http://localhost:8300/v2/health/ready`.
Tells the user to inspect `docker logs` for `ovms-service`, the model config at `ov_models/ovms/config.json`, and the matching model under `ov_models/ovms/openvino_models/`.

Includes at least one documented OVMS fix such as removing only the affected host-cached model with approval, lowering `PM_SUMMARIZATION_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS`, tuning `OVMS_CACHE_SIZE_GB`, or setting `VLM_TARGET_DEVICE=CPU`.

evals.prompt: I ran `source setup.sh --summary` and every container shows as up. The UI is reachable on port 12345 and the job gets created, but after I upload an MP4 the summary just sits in `Ready` or `In Progress` forever and no final summary ever appears. `video-ingestion` seems alive because `curl http://localhost:8090/pipelines` returns data. What should I check for this "everything is up but nothing happens" case?
evals.expected_output: A correct triage response uses `skills/vss-troubleshoot/scripts/triage.sh`, follows the documented dependency chain for missing summaries (`pipeline-manager` -> Postgres -> MinIO -> `video-ingestion` -> RabbitMQ -> `audio-analyzer` -> `ovms-service` or `vllm-cpu-service`), checks the relevant health endpoints and logs, and explains how stuck `Ready`/`In Progress` jobs often trace back to inference or downstream processing issues.
expectations: Mentions running `skills/vss-troubleshoot/scripts/triage.sh` before changing configuration.
Walks the documented summary triage order through `pipeline-manager`, `postgres-service`, `minio-service`, `video-ingestion`, `rabbitmq-service`, `audio-analyzer`, and the active inference backend.
References concrete health checks such as `http://localhost:3001/health`, `http://localhost:8090/pipelines`, and `http://localhost:8999/api/v1/health`.
Advises correlating stuck `Ready`/`In Progress` states with `ovms-service` or `vllm-cpu-service` logs rather than assuming the UI is the problem.
Includes at least one documented follow-up such as checking `PM_SUMMARIZATION_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS`, `VLM_MODEL_NAME`, or MinIO/RabbitMQ/Postgres health if all containers merely look up.

evals.prompt: Search mode boots, but every query says no videos found. `video-search` is running, while `vdms-dataprep` keeps logging "connection refused" to `vdms-vector-db:55555`, and `curl http://localhost:6016/v1/dataprep/health` fails. Can you triage this service-to-service connectivity problem and tell me what to verify before I wipe any data?
evals.expected_output: A correct triage response starts with `skills/vss-troubleshoot/scripts/triage.sh`, focuses on the search dependency chain (`video-search`, `vdms-dataprep`, `vdms-vector-db`, and `multimodal-embedding-serving` when API embedding mode is enabled), checks the documented health endpoints and logs for the failing services, and reserves re-ingest or `source setup.sh --clean-data` for cases where embedding dimensions or persisted state are actually the issue.
expectations: Mentions running `skills/vss-troubleshoot/scripts/triage.sh` and checking the search health endpoints `http://localhost:7890/health` and `http://localhost:6016/v1/dataprep/health`.
Identifies `vdms-vector-db` on port `55555` as a key dependency and tells the user to inspect `docker logs` for both `vdms-dataprep` and `vdms-vector-db`.
References `multimodal-embedding-serving` at `http://localhost:9777/health` when `EMBEDDING_PROCESSING_MODE=api`, and notes that `sdk` mode keeps embeddings inside `vdms-dataprep`.

Warns against jumping straight to `source setup.sh --clean-data` before fixing the connectivity issue, while still mentioning re-ingest or clean-data as the remedy for embedding-model dimension mismatches.

evals.prompt: I just ran `source setup.sh --summary --search` on my dev box and I can't reach the UI at `http://localhost:12345`. The browser just times out. I have some other Docker stuff running on this machine, so I'm wondering if a port is already taken. How do I check that and fix it?
evals.expected_output: A correct triage response runs `skills/vss-troubleshoot/scripts/triage.sh`, uses its documented host port checks to determine whether nginx/UI port `12345` or another published port is already bound, confirms whether `nginx` and `pipeline-manager` are healthy, and recommends freeing the conflicting process or overriding `APP_HOST_PORT` before redeploying.
expectations: Mentions running `skills/vss-troubleshoot/scripts/triage.sh` and reviewing its documented host port listener checks.
Identifies nginx/UI on host port `12345` as the primary gateway to check, and mentions `APP_HOST_PORT` as the override for that conflict.
Checks whether the `nginx` container started and uses `http://localhost:3001/health` as a direct Pipeline Manager health check when bypassing nginx is useful.
Recommends stopping the specific conflicting process or changing the relevant port environment variable before rerunning the intended `setup.sh` mode.

evals.prompt: After `source setup.sh --summary`, video-ingestion logs are full of MQTT connection errors and I can't tell if it's RabbitMQ or MinIO that's actually broken. Nothing ever reaches the summarization stage even though I uploaded a video 10 minutes ago. Can you help me figure out which of RabbitMQ, MinIO, or Postgres is the actual blocker here?
evals.expected_output: A correct triage response runs `skills/vss-troubleshoot/scripts/triage.sh`, follows the documented ingestion path through `video-ingestion`, RabbitMQ, MinIO, and Postgres, checks RabbitMQ MQTT/management ports and MinIO ports plus credentials, and distinguishes the first failing dependency before considering clean-data for confirmed corrupt persisted state.
expectations: Mentions running `skills/vss-troubleshoot/scripts/triage.sh` to collect Compose status, logs, port listeners, and environment-variable presence before changing configuration.
Checks `video-ingestion` at `http://localhost:8090/pipelines` and then inspects `rabbitmq-service`, `minio-service`, and `postgres-service` health/logs as documented summary dependencies.
References RabbitMQ ports `5672`, `15672`, and MQTT `1883`, MinIO ports `4001` and `4002`, and verifies `RABBITMQ_USER`/`RABBITMQ_PASSWORD` and `MINIO_ROOT_USER`/`MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD`.

Mentions `OD_MODEL_NAME` and object detection models under `ov_models/object-detection/ultralytics/public/<model>/FP32` as ingestion-stall checks, and reserves `source setup.sh --clean-data` for confirmed corrupt persisted state.

evals.prompt: I ran `source setup.sh --summary-and-search` and the containers all say they're up, but hitting `http://localhost:12345` in the browser just spins and `curl http://localhost:12345/manager/health` times out with no response at all. Can you figure out why the gateway isn't answering and what's actually broken?
evals.expected_output: Before triaging the gateway timeout, the skill unconditionally runs its bundled scripts/vss-bootstrap.sh, which checks the enclosing git repo's remote (origin/upstream) to see if it already points at the official open-edge-platform/edge-ai-libraries VSS repo or a fork of it and reuses that checkout if so, or otherwise performs a shallow, single-branch, sparse checkout of sample-applications/video-search-and-summarization from main, then cd's into the resolved app root before diagnosing the nginx/pipeline-manager health issue.
expectations: The answer runs the bundled bootstrap helper (scripts/vss-bootstrap.sh) as an unconditional first step, before addressing the gateway/health-check problem, even though the prompt never mentioned setup, location, or cloning.

The bootstrap check determines whether the current location is already a valid clone/checkout (or a fork) of the VSS project by inspecting the enclosing git repository's remote configuration (e.g. `git remote -v`, origin/upstream URL) to see if it points at the official open-edge-platform/edge-ai-libraries repo or a fork of it - not merely by checking for local marker files.
If that remote check finds a valid existing checkout (own clone or a fork whose remote traces back to the official repo), the answer states it is reused with NO re-clone performed.
If no valid checkout/remote is found, the answer performs a shallow, single-branch, sparse checkout limited to sample-applications/video-search-and-summarization from the main branch.
The answer changes directory (`cd "$APP_ROOT"`) into the resolved app root before running any of the skill's real diagnostic commands for the requested task.
